metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [Juli 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.38

context:
## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [Juli 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.38
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.38
- Datum: 07.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, we have been so glad to have your letter. It
is such a misery now with correspondence — from South
America all replies came so late, from my former wife I
have no reply and have sent her at least five cables; we try to
get her a visa and can not let her know, what she on her part
has to do. So we have all our lot of excitement and you can
imagine what a sad surprise it was to know that the first affi-
davit for Eva has not been sent off — we had been so happy to
have arranged it the second day of our arrival in (as we be-
lieved) perfect way.
Now I have a favour to ask you: please dont worry about
the house and if you prefer to stay in London let it entirely
to the care of the gardener. It is so indifferent, all those
private things and belongings, compared with the great issue
and I would have a bad feeling to think that you are sepa-
rated from your husband only to be the keeper of the house.
Whatever you do you will never hear a reproach from me
I know you do the best, but I would no sacrifice of your
part; it would prefer to let fall it to pieces.
We leave this week for Rio, I have already invitations
from Uruguay and Venezuela, but I will stay if possible
in Rio for some time. The distances are enormous and
we have to wait how things develop. I am so sorry that
we could not wait till to Evas arrival. Lotte has done
her best to find her a good stay — unfortunately most of
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Tinte violett. Die Zeile 'have no reply' enthält eine kleine Korrektur/Einfügung 'since' über der Zeile, die im Transkript als 'since' berücksichtigt wurde.

pages.transcription:
our friends are absent or out of town, — in September all
will be returned — and so I had not so much opportunity
of choice. Your idea that Evas children should travel
with her seemed first very attractive, but you should not
bother about such things. Most important is that she
comes over without waiting to long; ~~all~~ all will be
arranged for her and she must not bring over much of
her clothes and matters, perhaps a little music for her study
but in any case not much. I hope in your and our all
interest that she will not have to stay long in America and
can soon be united with you again — I can understand
what it means to tear over an only child over the ocean.
But as thousands of mothers do the same and the whole
world is full of sufferings we have no right to complain.
We have been here some five days and I have worked
enough, but not enough to forget the time. You may imagine
how we follow all news in the newspapers — and how we will
be more away than before, thousands and thousands of miles!
One more thing, dear Hannah, please dispose freely of all
I have and do not be too economical for you all, it has no
sense and I am only pleased to know that I am not too
much in your moral debt for all what you do. From
Rio we can communicate only by night-letters as mail
would take months and our dispositions depend from the
circumstances. The most desirable would be, we could take
back Eva with us very soon. Sincerely to you all yours
Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Tinte violett. Fortsetzung des Briefes.
Farbskala/Grauskala fuer Archivierung. Überlappt mit dem unteren Teil des Briefes (Seite 2).
